threads.title: The Cut
threads.intro: Establish what happened on stage and what the submission receipt does and does not prove.
threads.outcome_text: The demo ran 42 seconds against a two-minute cue, and Dev submitted the correct file on time.

threads.title: The File Trail
threads.intro: Follow the file from the kiosk to the player and test the custody theories against the records.
threads.outcome_text: The drive was returned with its seal intact, and the playback file was a 42-second export under the final filename.

threads.title: The Final Export
threads.intro: Combine the photo, the end card, the cue draft and the archive comparison.
threads.outcome_text: The photo, the rehearsal-only end card and the cue draft converge with the export record.

story_events.title: Forty-two seconds
story_events.body: Team Comet's demo stopped after 42 seconds although the approved cue called for 2:00. Dev's receipt shows he uploaded a two-minute file at 3:36 PM, before the cutoff. The receipt proves the submission, not what was later played.

story_events.title: A different file, the same name
story_events.body: The sealed drive was returned unopened, so Arjun's custody does not explain the mismatch. The workstation exported a 42-second file from the rehearsal cut under the name Comet_Final_v7.mp4 at 3:49 PM, under Nisha's account, and the player's checksum does not match Dev's upload.

story_events.title: The reflection and the draft
story_events.body: A reflection in the booth monitor places Nisha at the workstation while the export was running, the short file ends on a rehearsal-only note, and her cue draft says to use the short render. Dev's original is still in the kiosk archive, uncorrupted.
